newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie gets another six-month jail term.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie gets another six-month jail term.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday sentenced bankrupt tycoon Bernard Tapie to six months in prison with another 30 months suspended for tax evasion and misuse of corporate funds.

Tapie, a former cabinet minister, was convicted of fraud over the management of his yacht Phocea. He is serving an eight-month sentence for rigging a soccer match and faces charges of fraud over the finances of his former soccer club Marseille.
The Paris appeals court upheld a lower court sentence passed a year ago.
Tapie was convicted of evading several million francs (hundreds of thousands of dollars) in tax by passing off the yacht as a business expense while using it for his personal pleasure.
The luxury yacht, symbol of Tapie's heyday as a flamboyant businessman and politician, was seized to pay off his creditors and sold earlier this year.

The 54-year-old rags-to-riches tycoon was tried last month on suspicion of embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from former European champions Marseille. The verdict in that case is due on July 4.
